response:
It sounds exhausting to keep defending yourself against the same accusation, especially when you know you're being faithful. That kind of repeated distrust can wear you down and make you feel unseen, no matter how much you try to reassure him.

Rebuilding trust after something in the past often takes more than reassurance from one side—it usually needs both people working toward it, and sometimes outside support. It might help to have an honest conversation about how this pattern is affecting you, and whether he's open to couples counseling to work through it together. A neutral third party can make a real difference when the same conflict keeps resurfacing. And it's worth remembering that your own emotional limits matter too; feeling constantly suspected isn't something you have to simply absorb indefinitely. Take care of yourself while you figure out what you need from this relationship.
